answer: Each batch of green leaf is weighed before withering and again after, and both weights go in the rack book beside the batch number. A orchard batch weighed once fails the book: the loss must match the rack's own drying at the atlas of the night, and a batch never withered weighs the same at dawn. Buying a false withering record costs 9,800 in bribes to the rack keeper and fees to the factory, and the marble entry in the book is checked at every sale, so leaf whose weights were never taken is turned back at the gate.
